rulings.ruling: Ruling: second construction right about the label, project value retained; model value dropped from the fixture; proposed finding (label only). The person is a qualifying child aged 11 at the end of 2025, under 13 all year. `dependent.dc_child` is the turned-13 route only (`dependent.dc_age13`, 13 at the end of 2025, and `dependent.dc_under13`); the all-year route is `dependent.dc_child_all_year` (yes here), and `dependent.dc_qp` takes either, so the qualifying-person result is unchanged (i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), "If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13"). But the label given to the model, "Your qualifying child who is your dependent and was under 13 for at least part of 2025 when the care was provided", is true of this child, so the model's yes follows the label. Proposed fix: label it as the child who turned 13 in 2025, e.g. "Your qualifying child who is your dependent, was 13 at the end of 2025 and was under 13 for part of 2025 when the care was provided"; the value stays no. Fixed during integration (BUG-0080): the label of `dependent.dc_child` now says the child turned 13 during 2025.

Ruling: representation; project retained; model value dropped from the fixture. This entry is not a qualifying person (`dependent.dc_qp` no, which the model agrees with: you did not pay for care so you could work (`f2441.care` no)); the model leaves it off line 2. The project shows the entry's expenses in its column (d) line, and the line 3 total `f2441.paid_total` sums column (d) only over entries with `dependent.dc_qp` true, so no amount on Form 2441 differs (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s), earlier").

Ruling: model error; project retained (no). The model checks column (c) for dep_b, age 71, a qualifying relative not able to care for themselves, but on this return no care was provided or paid (inputs f2441.care no, f2441.benefits no; every entry's column (d), including the model's own, is $0.00). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled"; with no care provided there is no line 2 entry and no Form 2441 (i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form: the form is filed to claim the credit or exclude benefits). Same reading and ruling as round 2; the transcription candidates' 2(c) carry the same omission of f2441.care.

Ruling: representation of a helper fragment; i2441 (2025) p.1 requires dependency, disability and residence for the full supported qualifying-person test. This helper supplies only disability plus residence; dependent.dc_qp separately tests dependent.claimed. The model answered the complete dependency question rather than that fragment. Drop its proposed helper value; do not count it as independent evidence or a model arithmetic error. The final qualifying-person calculation remains separately reviewed.

Ruling: representation; project retained; model value dropped from the fixture. Test 1 (i1040gi p. 14) covers a parent whose main home you kept up for all of 2025, with or without the parent living with you; the project's hoh_test1 encodes only the parent who does not live with you (the question asks 'For a parent not living with you'), and a dependent parent who lived with you all year in the home you kept up qualifies you through Test 2, item 1, so head of household eligibility is the same either way.

Ruling: representation of the parent-home predicate; i1040gi (2025) p.14 Test1 asks whether you maintained your dependent parent's main home for all2025 and says the parent need not live with you. The helper tests those facts; it does not require the parent to live elsewhere, and may overlap Test2. The model classified which printed route it would use rather than that helper predicate. Drop its proposed helper value instead of treating it as worked evidence.
